newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bel-20 to rise on split between U.S. govt, Congress.
newsitem.headline: Bel-20 to rise on split between U.S. govt, Congress.

text.p: The Belgian Bel-20 share index stands to expand Tuesday's gain on the back of higher bonds and U.S. stocks and a firmer dollar with only some analysts seeing technical resistance emerging.
The Bel-20 gained almost half a percent to close at 1,810.36 points in moderately active trade.

Dealers said the bourse would benefit from optimism on Wall Street .DJI that the Democrat party would only supply a president but not control the Congress and thus jeopardise efforts to keep the deficit and inflation in check. First results are due shortly after polls close at 2300 GMT US-VOTE.
Wall Street saw selling pressure recently over worries Democrat control of the Senate, the House of Representatives and the presidency would give the party free rein.

Tuesday's session strengthened the Bel-20's hold above the psychologically important 1,800 level. A few analysts saw resistance at around 1,810, but most said more significant levels lay at 1,825-1,830.

Bel-20 heavyweight Petrofina had a choppy session, gaining, then paring gains, and ending just 0.1 percent higher on a company prediction that 1996 group earnings should be around 15 billion francs, up from 11.6 billion in 1995.

In an interview in Belgian newspaper De Standaard on Tuesday Petrofina CEO Francois Cornelis also said the group would ideally like to separate its Sigma paints division from its core petroleum and petrochemical businesses.
Analysts said the profit forecast was in line with expectations, but welcomed the news about low-margin Sigma.
A spokeswoman for PetroFina later said the company had no immediate plans for Sigma.
She also confirmed the company was looking to expand its retail petrol station network to Poland and Spain.

Retailer Delhaize recovered from an opening loss to gain 0.8 percent at 1,800. It was propped up by last week's news U.S. Food Lion unit was to buy Florida's Kash 'n Karry. Analysts said the move should boost 1997 earnings.
In the same sector Colruyt utperformed the index, rising 1.5 percent at 13,675.
Hamburger chain Quick extended Monday's 2.4 percent drop, slipping 2.2 percent to 1,990 francs as support at around 2,000 francs gave way.
